description: Cases for the command line. Start from a copy of contracts/ (or an empty directory when `empty` is true), write the lines of `ledger.<side>` to .ledger/<side>.jsonl, create a directory at .ledger/<side>.jsonl for every side in `ledgerDirectory` (it must still be a directory afterwards), then run the command with `args` and the environment variables of `env` (and no others). `exit` is the exit code; `stdout` and `stderr` are what the command writes to standard output and to standard error, character for character, without the newline at the end. When a case has `ledgerAfter`, .ledger/<side>.jsonl must afterwards hold exactly the lines of `ledgerAfter.<side>`, or not exist when that is null. In `args`, `env`, `stdout` and `stderr`, {dir} stands for the directory. In `stdout` and `stderr`, {tool} stands for the name of the executable (contract-fixtures in the TypeScript package, contract_fixtures in the Dart package), {version} for the version of the package, and {help} for the text of `help`, in which {tool} stands for the same name.
help:
{tool} — shared request/response fixtures that keep an API and its clients in step

Usage: {tool} <reset|check> --side <provider|consumer> [--dir <contracts>]
       {tool} summary [--dir <contracts>] [--depth <n>]

Commands:
  reset    Forget what earlier test runs of this side did. Run it before the tests.
  check    Fail unless this side's tests verified or read every fixture since the reset,
           and every fixture follows the format. Run it after all tests of this side.
  summary  Print one line per fixture: request, status, and the keys of the response body
           with their types. Does not touch the ledger.

Options:
  --side <provider|consumer>  The side whose tests ran. Not for summary
  --dir <contracts>           The contracts directory: the one that holds provider/, consumer/
                              and tables/, not the directory of a package
                              (default: the environment variable CONTRACT_FIXTURES_DIR)
  --depth <n>                 For summary: how many levels of objects in the response body
                              to open, 1 to 9 (default: 1, the keys at the top)
  -h, --help                  Show this help
  -v, --version               Show the version

Exit codes: 0 no problems, 1 problems found (summary: no fixtures) or the command could
not finish, 2 wrong usage

cases.case: --help prints the help
-h is the same, also after a command
--version prints the version and nothing else
-v is the same, also after a command
reset removes the ledger of this side and leaves the other side's
reset of a side without a ledger
check leaves the ledgers as they are
cases.stdout: {tool} check (provider side): OK (4 fixture(s), all verified or read by this side's tests)

cases.case: an option given twice: the last one counts
cases.stdout: {tool} check (provider side): OK (4 fixture(s), all verified or read by this side's tests)

cases.case: --help after wrong usage is too late
--help before wrong usage wins
wrong usage: an empty value for --dir
wrong usage: an empty value for --side
wrong usage: a value for --version
wrong usage: the side is looked at before the directory
wrong usage: the value of an option may start with a hyphen
check: this side did everything

{tool} check (consumer side): 4 problem(s) in 4 fixture(s)
  - none of the 4 fixture(s) that follow the format was verified or read by the consumer side's tests (they are not listed one by one)
Hint: .ledger/consumer.jsonl does not exist, but .ledger/provider.jsonl has some. Did the consumer side's tests run, and is consumer the side to check?
Run `{tool} reset` and the consumer side's tests before this check.

Run `{tool} reset` and the provider side's tests before this check.
